query: integration constraints for For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements. It applies that strategy by the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. It admits at most the count the caller passes, in that rank order, and places every candidate it does not admit into deferred, preserving their order in the candidate list. Each candidate keeps its source_index. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices are written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the split is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped and write the same two lists on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. The user named which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, ordered by that first-maximum rule, on the pose result the handling process reads. in src
findings: Rank with the same strict-weak comparator select_detection already passes to std::max_element. highest_confidence orders by score then area; largest_area orders by area then score. Equivalence is both directions false, so a full tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tie stays deferred. A comparator that uses <= is not a strict weak ordering. std::sort, std::partial_sort, and std::nth_element do not preserve equivalent order and can admit the later tie. std::stable_sort does preserve it, but the tail of that sort is rank order, not candidate-list order, so it is not the deferred vector.

An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty. std::max_element on an empty range returns last, so do not dereference it. An unknown strategy throws std::invalid_argument and is not turned into a failure diagnostic. Resolve the empty list before the strategy check, so a capture with no class-matched detections still returns empty and the node early return that publishes nothing stays that return.

Admitted holds at most the caller count, in first-maximum rank order. Deferred holds every candidate not admitted, in original candidate-list order. std::stable_partition would keep both sides in input order, so the admitted side would not be rank order. Copy each candidate, including source_index. That index is the slot in Detection2DArray.detections, not the position in the candidate vector and not Detection2D.id, which is a cross-message string and may be empty. Empty results and a non-target class are already absent, so the indices can have gaps. Do not score the ObjectHypothesis list again; the candidate already keeps the highest hypothesis score and class_id.

The pose node passes its detection_selection strategy and a count of one. Admitted then has one candidate, and that candidate is the only pallet the single stage-2 estimate runs on, using that candidate source_index. Passing the candidate-list length would admit everyone and leave deferred empty. A larger count than the list admits every candidate in rank order and leaves deferred empty. Deferred candidates are not estimated. Python max returns the first maximal item, so this admitted candidate is that same first maximum.

Append int32 admitted_source_index and int32[] deferred_source_indices after input_depth_stamp. int32 is int32_t, and int32[] is an unbounded sequence, not a fixed array. Field names are lowercase words separated by underscores. Do not reorder or retype the fields already on the message. geometry_msgs/PoseStamped is a header and a pose, so the plain pose cannot carry the split. Slot 0 is a real detection. Write the admitted index on every rich publish. An empty deferred sequence means no other class-matched candidate. Leave accepted, quality_reasons, and failure_reason as they are. The success split is these two fields on PalletPoseStamped, the pose result the handling process reads.

input_rgb_stamp is the detection-array header, which should match the image that produced the detections, and input_depth_stamp is the paired depth header. PalletPoseStamped.header.stamp stays the publish time. setMaxIntervalDuration rejects a pair whose stamps differ by more than the configured interval, so the two capture stamps can still differ inside that interval. The two admission vectors are this pair only. builtin_interfaces/Time nanosec is in [0, 1e9).

When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped. The only result is the existing DiagnosticStatus at WARN (byte value 1). KeyValue is one string key and one string value, so admitted_source_index is decimal text and deferred_source_indices is one comma-separated string in deferred order. StatusItem::getValue returns the first value stored for a key, so a repeated key hides the list. Keep the status name, hardware id, failure_reason, status message, and both stamp keys. Encode each stamp as seconds, a dot, and nanosec padded to 9. An empty deferred list is an empty string. DiagnosticArray.header.stamp stays the publish clock. The analyzer sets the group level to the max child level, so this remains one WARN status. The success split is not carried only on an OK diagnostic.

The empty-candidate return and the depth-conversion exception return publish nothing. Building the two vectors does not add a publish there: the first has no admitted slot, and the second has no converted depth pair. A publisher depth of 10 is keep-last, reliable, and volatile. A best-effort publisher does not match a reliable subscription. Keep-last drops whole messages, so one PalletPoseStamped carries both index fields and both capture stamps.
